sources.note: Builds a Parkinson's screen from control data alone using a contrastive activation direction derived from synthetically degraded healthy speech and a nearest-neighbour anomaly score in face-encoder space, and gives a measurable precondition -- positive cosine between the synthetic and real disease directions -- that predicts in advance which modality the steering primitive will work on.
sources.title: Label-Free Parkinson's Disease Screening from Face and Voice through Mechanistic Interpretability

sources.note: Turns the hidden-role game Avalon into a diagnostic instrument rather than an arena, decomposing theory of mind into a 2x2 taxonomy of perspective-constrained binary statements, and shows by probing, ground-truth injection and steering that models represent the right answer internally while failing to say it.
sources.title: Avalon-ToM-Bench: Evaluating Fine-Grained Theory of Mind via Asymmetric Game Mechanics

sources.note: Puts an ensemble of LLM judges between a robot-autonomy planner and its execution layer as gating middleware that accepts, rejects or escalates each plan to human review, and reports that ensemble size barely moves accuracy while the errors concentrate at the escalate boundary rather than between accept and reject.
sources.title: Agentic Harnesses: LLM-Driven Verification Layers for Robot Autonomy

result.definition: When one label dominates an evaluation set, so that accuracy stops being informative and a metric can be satisfied by a degenerate rule. All three sources here treat it as something to design around rather than to report. The Parkinson's screen has 13 percent prevalence, at which predicting all-healthy already scores 0.87, so it reports AUROC, F1 and negative predictive value at a Youden-optimal operating point instead, and reads its own result as a rule-out triage screen (NPV 0.95) rather than as a diagnostic (PPV 0.35). The theory-of-mind benchmark takes the opposite approach and removes the problem by construction, balancing the set at roughly 50 percent TRUE per ability precisely so that a residual TRUE/FALSE prior shows up as a gap between accuracy and macro-F1 -- and its steering result is then read through class-conditional recall, where a model moves from a degenerate 10.7/98.0 to a balanced 73.8/80.2, a change accuracy alone would have attributed to competence rather than to threshold. The robot-plan verification work shows what happens without either precaution: with reject holding 31 of 38 cases, the authors state that per-class precision and recall are not stable and substitute aggregate deployment-aligned metrics. Together the sources make one point: the imbalance determines which metric can be read at all, and choosing it afterwards is choosing the conclusion.
